title: CompGen: A Conditional Generation Framework for Inverse Composition Design of Catalytic Surfaces
experiments_summary: The paper performs several experimental procedures: (1) CIAE Pretraining: The Chemically Informed Autoencoder is pretrained in two stages on a subset of the OC20 dataset (131,740 adsorption configurations of 13 adsorbates on surfaces with up to three elements). Stage I uses a VGG-like CNN backbone pretrained on the Materials Project dataset for binary classification to initialize the encoder. Stage II trains the full autoencoder end-to-end using MSE loss for shell-wise composition reconstruction. Performance is assessed via MSE of latent reconstruction and cosine similarity between reconstructed and ground-truth 118-dimensional composition vectors for both shells, evaluated on held-out OC20 and out-of-domain HEA test sets. (2) OC20 Pretraining of Conditional Diffusion Model: A conditional latent diffusion model is pretrained on the OC20 subset using both U-Net and Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbones, conditioned on adsorbate type (one-hot, 13 classes), adsorption energy (scalar), and element list (allowed element types per shell). (3) Fine-tuning on HEA Dataset: The pretrained CompGen model is fine-tuned on the HEA dataset (4,892 configurations of *OH and *O on five-element Ag/Ir/Pd/Pt/Ru surfaces, 80:10:10 split) using two strategies: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and full-parameter fine-tuning, to assess transferability and adaptability. (4) Baseline Comparison: A chemically agnostic baseline is constructed by zero-padding and reshaping composition vectors into a 48x48 spatial grid without chemical priors, feeding directly into the DiT diffusion model, bypassing the CIAE entirely. (5) Data Efficiency Study: A systematic ablation is conducted using 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100% of the training data to evaluate data scaling behavior, measured by MSE and cosine similarity on both OC20 and HEA tasks. (6) Evaluation Metrics: All generative models are evaluated using Fréchet Distance (FD) between real and generated latent distributions, Leakage (fraction of generated composition falling outside allowed element sets), and Cosine Similarity (point-wise alignment between generated and ground-truth composition vectors).
